items.stem: What role does the partition key play in a Kinesis Data Stream?

options.text: It determines which shard a record goes to and preserves per-key ordering
options.rationale: Correct: the partition key maps records to shards and orders records per key.
Encryption is separate from the partition key.

options.text: It sets the data retention period
options.rationale: Retention is a stream setting, not the partition key.
Records persist for the retention window.

items.explanation: Correct: the partition key maps records to shards and orders them per key.

items.stem: When is Kinesis Data Firehose a better fit than consuming a Data Stream directly?

options.text: When you want managed, near-real-time delivery to destinations like S3 with little code
options.rationale: Correct: Firehose is managed delivery with buffering and transforms.

options.text: When you need sub-second, record-level custom processing
options.rationale: That calls for Data Streams with a custom consumer.

options.text: When you must never store the data
When ordering per key must be guaranteed to a custom app
options.rationale: Fine-grained ordering control is a Data Streams concern.

items.explanation: Correct: Firehose suits managed near-real-time delivery.

items.stem: Which TWO help avoid a hot shard and throttling in Kinesis Data Streams? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Choose a high-cardinality partition key that spreads load
options.rationale: Correct: a well-distributed key balances records across shards.

options.text: Reshard or scale shards as throughput grows
Send all records with a single constant partition key
options.rationale: A constant key concentrates load on one shard.

items.explanation: Correct: spread load with a good key and scale shards.
